**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/23 (Tue) 06:49
- [USER] User inquired about pet food regulations in Europe.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Pet foods require pre-market authorization in Europe before they can be sold to consumers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] This requirement is under Regulation (EC) No. 767/2009 on the placing on the market and use of feed.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Pet food manufacturers must submit an application for authorization of their products to the competent authority in the EU member state where they intend to market the product.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The application must include information about the product's composition, labeling, and intended use.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The application must also include data demonstrating that the product is safe and nutritious for the target species.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The competent authority will review the application and may request additional information or testing before granting or denying authorization.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Once a product is authorized, it can be marketed and sold throughout the EU.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In addition to pre-market authorization, pet food manufacturers in Europe must comply with ongoing requirements for labeling, traceability, and safety.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] These requirements are enforced by national authorities and can include inspections of manufacturing facilities and product samples.
